pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Where can you find correct interjections for your mother tongue? (1 mark)
   A. By guessing
   B. By inventing them
   C. By listening to and asking elders and teachers
   D. By copying from another language

2. The bag is below the table. Which preposition fits? (1 mark)
   A. under
   B. between
   C. beside
   D. on

3. Which is the correct order for washing hands? (1 mark)
   A. Rinse, dry, wet, soap
   B. Soap, dry, wet, rinse
   C. Dry, wet, soap, rinse
   D. Wet, rub soap, rinse, dry

4. A good ending to an imaginative story usually (1 mark)
   A. repeats the title
   B. starts a new problem always
   C. solves the problem or shows the lesson
   D. has no full stops

5. Which is a polite way to interrupt? (1 mark)
   A. Be quiet!
   B. Excuse me, may I say something?
   C. Stop talking!
   D. You are wrong!

6. What should each step in written instructions usually start with? (1 mark)
   A. A number only
   B. A name
   C. A colour
   D. A verb

7. What are non-verbal cues in a performance? (1 mark)
   A. Written words
   B. Loud shouting
   C. Gestures and facial expressions
   D. Music only

8. In the sentence Oops, it is torn, what is the interjection? (1 mark)
   A. torn
   B. Oops
   C. is
   D. it

9. What is the plural of the English word cup? (1 mark)
   A. cupes
   B. cups
   C. cuppies
   D. cup's

10. What is a good first step when reading for information? (1 mark)
   A. Guess the ending
   B. Close the book
   C. Ask what you want to find out
   D. Copy the title

11. Where do oral narratives come from? (1 mark)
   A. From nowhere
   B. From only one book
   C. From machines only
   D. From elders and storytellers who pass them on

12. What should you do with the events of a story you tell? (1 mark)
   A. Skip the beginning
   B. Never mention the end
   C. Mix them up
   D. Tell them in the order they happened

13. A noun is a word that (1 mark)
   A. names a person, animal, place or thing
   B. describes a colour only
   C. joins two sentences
   D. shows an action

14. A saying such as It is raining cats and dogs means (1 mark)
   A. animals are falling
   B. the weather is cold
   C. it is raining very heavily
   D. dogs and cats are lost

15. Which sentence is a simile? (1 mark)
   A. She is as bright as the sun.
   B. She is a sun.
   C. She is bright.
   D. She is a shining star.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Explain how the meaning of You are coming to school changes when it is a statement and when it is a question. (3 marks)

17. Write a five-line role play dialogue on personal safety between a child and a stranger. Show the speaker names and use question marks correctly. (5 marks)

18. Describe how you would scan a passage to find how much a box of mangoes costs. (4 marks)

19. List three steps for skimming. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #6 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — By listening to and asking elders and teachers
   Speakers know the correct forms.

2. A — under
   Under means below something.

3. D — Wet, rub soap, rinse, dry
   This is the logical order.

4. C — solves the problem or shows the lesson
   Endings resolve the story.

5. B — Excuse me, may I say something?
   It asks permission politely.

6. D — A verb
   Steps begin with action words.

7. C — Gestures and facial expressions
   Non-verbal cues are actions without words.

8. B — Oops
   Oops shows a small mistake.

9. B — cups
   Most English nouns add s to make the plural.

10. C — Ask what you want to find out
   A question in mind helps you look for the right facts.

11. D — From elders and storytellers who pass them on
   They are passed on by word of mouth.

12. D — Tell them in the order they happened
   Order helps listeners follow.

13. A — names a person, animal, place or thing
   Nouns are naming words.

14. C — it is raining very heavily
   It is an expression for heavy rain.

15. A — She is as bright as the sun.
   It uses as to compare.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: As a statement the voice falls and it tells something. As a question the voice rises and it asks something.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of the two meanings and one mark for the voice movement.

17. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any five correct lines, for example Child: Good afternoon. Stranger: Do you want a ride? Child: No, thank you. I will wait for my mother. Stranger: Are you sure? Child: Yes, I am telling my teacher.
   Working / marking points: One mark for speaker names, one for a safe message, one for correct questions and two for five clear lines.

18. (4 marks)
   Answer: Know that you are looking for the price, run your eyes over the text looking for numbers, stop at the number, read the sentence around it and check that it answers the question.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four steps.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read the title, read headings, read the first sentence of each paragraph, glance over the rest, say the main idea.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.
